patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 00/22] mm: introduce N_MEMORY_COMMON

series_items.subject: [PATCH 01/22] mm: add node-state-filtered zone and node iterators
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds helper functions and macros to the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) subsystem, allowing MM walkers to select node eligibility explicitly. It introduces node-state-filtered zone and node iterators using bitmap intersection helpers without allocating temporary nodemasks. The patch includes new functions for iterating over zones on nodes in a specific state and defines several macros for simplifying these iterations.

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng questioned the consistency of two helper functions in the patch: for_each_zone_node_state and for_each_populated_zone_state, noting that the latter uses a single statement with an if/else form to avoid a -Wdangling-else warning, while the former is split into two separate functions. He asked whether the warning was significant enough to warrant keeping the current implementation or changing for_each_populated_zone_state to match.
review_comments.raw_body:
A question on consistency. This one is a single for statement, with 2 new helper functions.
for_each_populated_zone_state() in the same patch uses "if (!cond) ; else" form instead.

Both forms keep a caller's else correct. The only difference I can find is that the if/else
form give a -Wdangling-else warning when the loop is the unbraced body of an if.

Is that the reason for the 2 helper function here? If the warning doesn't matter, this could
use the same short form and drop the 2 functions. If it does matter, should
for_each_populated_zone_state() be a single statement too ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledges a warning from checks and plans to re-examine and possibly restructure their code, specifically considering using a different shape or avoiding the existing pattern.
review_comments.raw_body:
Yeah I was getting that warning from various checks. I'd convinced
byself this was a false-positive, but it does look very funky indeed.

Let me look into this again, it's possible I can massage this better to
use the short form still.  It's also possible that I should just use a
different shape entirely than trying to use the existing pattern.

-- 
~Gregory

series_items.subject: [PATCH 02/22] mm: publish and clear node memory states via helpers
series_items.patch_summary: This patch centralizes the updates of node memory states in Linux kernel by introducing two new functions, `node_set_memory_state` and `node_clear_memory_state`, which replace the existing separate calls to set or clear individual memory states (N_MEMORY, N_NORMAL_MEMORY, and N_HIGH_MEMORY). The behavior remains unchanged. This change aims to simplify the code and make it more maintainable.

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that the patch introduces additional cache pressure due to up to three set_bit() calls on node_states[], which is __read_mostly, and suggested adding a test-before-set in the helper or addressing this in the commit message.
review_comments.raw_body:
Um, so I am not sure how much cache pressure this will add, I assume it's small ?

Just want to point out that the old code only wrote these bits for a node's first
memory. THis now does up to 3 set_bit() calls on node_states[] for every onlined block.
The result is the same, but node_states[] is __read_mostly. A test-before-set in the helper
would keep the old behavior, or if you would like to keep it, please address in commit message.

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that setting N_MEMORY in hotplug code could lead to a race condition, agreed to add a test before setting new state and early-out if necessary.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hotplug isn't on a particular hot path, but I can test N_MEMORY before
setting any new state and just early-out.  That would keep the behavior.

-- 
~Gregory

series_items.subject: [PATCH 03/22] mm: introduce the common-memory node state
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces the concept of 'common memory' in Linux, which allows nodes to be identified as having memory that can be managed by the kernel's MM services without requiring explicit node requests. It adds a new state, N_MEMORY_COMMON, and exposes this information via sysfs attributes. The patch also updates documentation and APIs to reflect these changes.

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that the patch description does not clearly distinguish between common memory (N_MEMORY_COMMON) and private memory, requesting a clearer distinction to be made.
review_comments.raw_body:
This sentense kind of blurred me, you state that N_MEMORY_COMMON is meant
to isolate the concept of #2 from N_MEMORY, I expect something
making clear distinction between common memory and private memory ?

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that N_MEMORY and N_MEMORY_COMMON are initially equivalent, but plans to introduce a new state (N_MEMORY_PRIVATE) in v6 of the patch series, which will make the sets disjoint.
review_comments.raw_body:
Sorry, basically as of this set:
  node_state[N_MEMORY] == node_state[N_MEMORY_COMMON]

Later, we'll introduce N_MEMORY_PRIVATE and the sets become disjoint.

I realize posting this series in isolation was a mistake now, and I am
going to post the entire v6 of private nodes with the reworks you
suggested instead.

-- 
~Gregory

series_items.subject: [PATCH 04/22] mm/page_alloc: build zonelists from common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the way zonelists are built in the Linux kernel's memory management system. Instead of building fallback lists for all nodes and local lists only for non-common nodes, it builds common memory zonelists from N_MEMORY_COMMON and local-only zonelists for common nodes. This change is achieved by refactoring the build_local_zonelist function to reuse code for building a local-only zonelist for nodes outside the common set. The patch does not affect nodes with no memory, as they do not have zones to list anyway.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 05/22] mm/mempolicy: keep interleave and tmpfs mount policies on common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory policy code to use a new set of common memory nodes (N_MEMORY_COMMON) instead of N_MEMORY for boot memory policy calculations and their per-node sysfs entries. It also restricts the node set applied by mpol_set_nodemask() and mbind() masks to N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes, ensuring that only eligible nodes are considered for memory policies. This change is intended to simplify the code and improve performance, but does not introduce any immediate behavior changes since all memory is initially common.

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng questioned whether it's assumed that all common memory nodes are online, potentially invalidating the patch's logic for restricting node sets.
review_comments.raw_body:
Maybe I overlooked or somehow, but when do we have the assumption
that common memory is definitely onlined ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that the code's behavior at init time makes checking N_MEMORY_COMMON unnecessary and agreed that existing code could simply check N_MEMORY for the same result.
review_comments.raw_body:
For this particular case it's not particularly relevant.

This code only runs at init time, so it's either got memory or it
doesn't.  If the memory is present but offline, it still wants weights.

There isn't really a bug here, but the existing code could also just
check N_MEMORY and end up with the same result.  If the memory is
hotplugged later, it still gets weights accordingly.

-- 
~Gregory

series_items.subject: [PATCH 06/22] mm: base hash distribution on common memory nodes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the hash distribution mechanism to base its decisions on common memory nodes, rather than all memory nodes. This change is made by counting the number of common memory nodes when applying a single-node optimization. As all memory is currently considered common, the behavior remains unchanged.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 07/22] mm/memory_hotplug: migrate offlined pages to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the memory hotplug migration code to restrict the destination nodes for page migration to only those that are marked as N_MEMORY_COMMON. This change prevents the destination nodemask from becoming empty when migrating pages to a node that is not an eligible allocation target, which can occur in certain configurations where some nodes are marked as N_MEMORY but not N_MEMORY_COMMON.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 08/22] mm/memory-tiers: restrict demotion topology to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the demotion topology in Linux's memory-tiers to only consider common memory (N_MEMORY_COMMON). It achieves this by modifying several functions that build demotion paths and assign nodes to memory tiers, ensuring that these operations are limited to nodes within N_MEMORY_COMMON. This change does not affect existing behavior for nodes carrying N_MEMORY_COMMON, as all current nodes do so. The patch aims to improve the management of memory allocation and demotion in the Linux kernel by reducing unnecessary complexity and potential issues related to non-common memory nodes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 09/22] mm/ksm: restrict merging to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the merging of memory pages to only common memory, excluding ZONE_DEVICE folios and non-anonymous memory. The change is made in two locations where KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging) service acquires memory pages. This ensures that KSM does not attempt to merge memory outside the ordinary memory pool, which aligns with its opportunistic nature.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 10/22] mm/khugepaged: restrict collapse to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the collapse operation in the mm/khugepaged module to only common memory, which is memory that can be shared between processes. The existing checks for zone device pages are replaced with a check for common memory using the page_is_common_memory() function. Additionally, a new check is added to the collapse_scan_file() function to ensure that page-cache folios are also restricted to common memory.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 11/22] mm/mempolicy: don't NUMA-hint folios outside common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NUMA balancing scanner to not inject hint faults or migrate folios that are outside of common memory, which includes zone device memory. The existing check for zone device memory is replaced with a more general check for common memory. As all memory is considered common at this point, the behavior remains unchanged.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 12/22] mm/damon: restrict DAMON-native folio operations to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts DAMON-native folio operations to common memory, preventing them from being performed on memory outside of N_MEMORY_COMMON. This change treats these folios like ZONE_DEVICE memory and prevents DAMON from acquiring or aging them. As a result, virtual address monitoring will report accessed pages as such, and migration is restricted to destinations within N_MEMORY_COMMON.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 13/22] mm/hugetlb: restrict pool growth to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the growth of HugeTLB pools to nodes that have common memory (N_MEMORY_COMMON). It achieves this by changing the allocation mask in several functions, ensuring that new pool folios are only allocated on these nodes. This change will cause hugepage allocations to fail on nodes without N_MEMORY_COMMON. The original allowed mask for pool shrinking and demotion is preserved to allow existing pool folios to still be found on any online-memory node.

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that the new code may lead to an uneven or smaller pool size due to delayed node allocation, and suggested moving the nodes_and() call inside the loop to restore the original behavior.
review_comments.raw_body:
For a global request the caller passes &node_states[N_MEMORY], so before this patch
the grow loop read the live mask on every alloc_pool_huge_folio().
Now the mask is sampled once, before the loop.

The loop drops hugetlb_lock and can run for a long time. If a node gets its first
memoroy in that window, the old code would start using it. The new code won't, until
the next write to nr_hugepages.

So the pool can end up uneven, or smaller than requested if the other nodes are full.

I think the nodes_and() should be placed inside the loop to keep the old behavior ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged a potential issue with hugepage distribution when there's a race between hugetlb allocation and memory hotplug, but downplayed its significance as an 'innocuous corner case'. They agreed to retain the old behavior if it's reliable.
review_comments.raw_body:
I can make the adjustment, but the concern is that previously we'd
start spreading the distribution of hugepages differently when there's a
race between hugetlb allocation and memory hotplug?

That seems like a pretty innocuous corner case to be worried about.

I can see about retaining the old behavior, but i'm not sure what you're
describing is reliable behavior already.

-- 
~Gregory

series_items.subject: [PATCH 14/22] mm/page_alloc: count common memory nodes for kswapd recovery
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of free_frozen_page_commit() to only clear kswapd hopeless state when there is more than one common memory node, rather than any memory node. This change ensures that direct reclaim is triggered even if allocations fall back to another node without triggering it initially. The patch does not alter behavior since all memory is considered common at this point.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 15/22] mm/oom_kill: compare OOM constraints against common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the OOM (Out of Memory) killer's behavior to compare policy and cpuset constraints against common memory, rather than all memory. This change ensures that nodes outside the common memory zone do not artificially inflate the constrained capacity or make global policies appear constrained. The modification is made in the mm/oom_kill.c file and does not affect behavior when all memory is considered common.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 16/22] tty/sysrq: use common memory for the manual OOM zonelist
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the manual OOM (Out-Of-Memory) zonelist in the sysrq driver to use common memory instead of every node that has memory. This change ensures that the fallback domain for ordinary allocations contains only common memory, which is a more accurate representation of the system's available resources. The behavior remains unchanged because all nodes are considered common at this point.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 17/22] mm/vmscan: restrict reclaim to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the reclaim process to common memory, which is a type of memory that can be shared among multiple nodes in a system. The changes include starting kswapd only on common nodes at boot or hotplug time, walking only common zones during direct reclaim and throttling, and using common nodes when MGLRU registers an mm or iterates/validates nodes. This approach ensures that the reclaim process is more efficient and effective by focusing on memory that can be easily shared and reclaimed.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 18/22] mm/compaction: restrict compaction to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the compaction process in Linux to common memory only, which is a subset of all available memory. The changes include modifying the kcompactd daemon to start on common nodes at boot and hotplug, limiting direct compaction to common zones, and restricting proactive compaction to common nodes. This approach aims to improve system performance by focusing compaction efforts on areas where it will have the most impact.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 19/22] mm/migrate: restrict move_pages() destinations to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the destination of the move_pages() function to common memory, rejecting any node without common memory. This change aligns with how memory policies work and ensures that user memory is placed on a general-purpose node. Currently, all memory is considered common, so this patch does not introduce any behavioral changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 20/22] PM: hibernate: size the image from common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the hibernation image size calculation to only count free pages in zones on nodes that are marked as common memory, rather than all populated zones. This ensures that the hibernation image can be stored in common memory. The patch also separates the image metadata estimate from the page frame tracking, which is still calculated for all populated zones.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 21/22] mm/khugepaged: base the recommended min_free_kbytes on common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adjusts the calculation for recommended min_free_kbytes in the khugepaged module to reserve memory only on nodes that are marked as N_MEMORY_COMMON, which represents common memory. This change helps THP allocations avoid fragmentation by reserving two pageblocks per populated zone on these nodes. The recommendation remains unchanged for all other nodes with memory.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 22/22] nodemask: remove the now-unused first_memory_node/next_memory_node
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes two unused helper functions, first_memory_node and next_memory_node, from the Linux kernel's nodemask code. These functions were previously used to get the first or next node in a specific state, but their usage has been replaced by explicit naming of the desired state. The removal of these helpers forces new code to explicitly choose a node state instead of silently defaulting to N_MEMORY.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch introduces the concept of 'common memory' as a separate entity from NUMA nodes that have memory, allowing for private node memory to be isolated from the main memory management system. The patch creates a new flag N_MEMORY_COMMON and converts existing users of N_MEMORY to use this new flag instead. This is the first phase of a series that aims to introduce private NUMA nodes and allow userland to manage them via mbind() and migrate_pages().

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the lack of explicit node eligibility filtering in MM walkers by adding helper functions/macros to select node eligibility explicitly, and iterators for nodemask intersection and state iteration without allocating temporary nodemasks.
review_comments.raw_body:
Add node-state-filter helper functions/macros so MM walkers can select
their node eligibility explicitly.

Add nodemask intersection and nodemask/state iterators using the bitmap
intersection helpers, without allocating a temporary nodemask.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 include/linux/mmzone.h   | 46 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 include/linux/nodemask.h | 28 ++++++++++++++++++++----
 2 files changed, 70 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

diff --git a/include/linux/mmzone.h b/include/linux/mmzone.h
index c161d563ce8fd..5ff190d870830 100644
--- a/include/linux/mmzone.h
+++ b/include/linux/mmzone.h
@@ -1845,6 +1845,13 @@ extern struct zone *next_zone(struct zone *zone);
 			; /* do nothing */		\
 		else
 
+/* Populated zones on nodes in @state. */
+#define for_each_populated_zone_state(zone, state)	\
+	for_each_populated_zone(zone)			\
+		if (!node_state(zone_to_nid(zone), state))	\
+			; /* do nothing */		\
+		else
+
 static inline struct zone *zonelist_zone(struct zoneref *zoneref)
 {
 	return zoneref->zone;
@@ -1937,6 +1944,45 @@ static inline struct zoneref *first_zones_zonelist(struct zonelist *zonelist,
 			zone = zonelist_zone(z))
 
 
+static inline struct zoneref *
+next_zones_zonelist_state(struct zoneref *z, enum zone_type highest_zoneidx,
+			  const nodemask_t *nodes, enum node_states state)
+{
+	z = next_zones_zonelist(z, highest_zoneidx, nodes);
+	while (zonelist_zone(z) && !node_state(zonelist_node_idx(z), state))
+		z = next_zones_zonelist(++z, highest_zoneidx, nodes);
+	return z;
+}
+
+static inline struct zoneref *
+first_zones_zonelist_state(struct zonelist *zonelist,
+			   enum zone_type highest_zoneidx,
+			   const nodemask_t *nodes, enum node_states state)
+{
+	return next_zones_zonelist_state(zonelist->_zonerefs, highest_zoneidx,
+					 nodes, state);
+}
+
+/**
+ * for_each_zone_node_state - iterate zones in intersect(nodemask, node_state(state))
+ * @zone: The current zone in the iterator
+ * @z: The current pointer within zonelist->_zonerefs being iterated
+ * @zlist: The zonelist being iterated
+ * @highidx: The zone index of the highest zone to return
+ * @nodemask: Nodemask allowed by the allocator
+ * @state: The node state the zone's node must be in
+ *
+ * The state filter is part of the iteration rather than a trailing if, so that
+ * this expands to a single for statement: a macro ending in an unbraced if
+ * silently steals a following else from the caller.
+ */
+#define for_each_zone_node_state(zone, z, zlist, highidx, nodemask, state)	\
+	for (z = first_zones_zonelist_state(zlist, highidx, nodemask, state),	\
+		zone = zonelist_zone(z);					\
+		zone;								\
+		z = next_zones_zonelist_state(++z, highidx, nodemask, state),	\
+		zone = zonelist_zone(z))
+
 /**
  * for_each_zone_zonelist - helper macro to iterate over valid zones in a zonelist at or below a given zone index
  * @zone: The current zone in the iterator
diff --git a/include/linux/nodemask.h b/include/linux/nodemask.h
index 607373bd83ee6..28a456c3f5964 100644
--- a/include/linux/nodemask.h
+++ b/include/linux/nodemask.h
@@ -386,6 +386,10 @@ static __always_inline void __nodes_fold(nodemask_t *dstp, const nodemask_t *ori
 	for ((node) = 0; (node) < 1 && !nodes_empty(mask); (node)++)
 #endif /* MAX_NUMNODES */
 
+/* Iterate the nodes present in both masks without a temporary nodemask. */
+#define for_each_node_mask_and(node, mask1, mask2) \
+	for_each_and_bit(node, nodes_addr(mask1), nodes_addr(mask2), MAX_NUMNODES)
+
 /*
  * Bitmasks that are kept for all the nodes.
  */
@@ -411,6 +415,10 @@ enum node_states {
 
 extern nodemask_t node_states[NR_NODE_STATES];
 
+/* Iterate the nodes in a mask that also belong to the specified state. */
+#define for_each_node_mask_state(node, mask, state) \
+	for_each_node_mask_and(node, mask, node_states[state])
+
 #if MAX_NUMNODES > 1
 static __always_inline int node_state(int node, enum node_states state)
 {
@@ -435,15 +443,21 @@ static __always_inline int num_node_state(enum node_states state)
 #define for_each_node_state(__node, __state) \
 	for_each_node_mask((__node), node_states[__state])
 
-#define first_online_node	first_node(node_states[N_ONLINE])
-#define first_memory_node	first_node(node_states[N_MEMORY])
+#define first_node_state(state)	first_node(node_states[state])
+static __always_inline unsigned int next_node_state(int nid, enum node_states state)
+{
+	return next_node(nid, node_states[state]);
+}
+
+#define first_online_node	first_node_state(N_ONLINE)
+#define first_memory_node	first_node_state(N_MEMORY)
 static __always_inline unsigned int next_online_node(int nid)
 {
-	return next_node(nid, node_states[N_ONLINE]);
+	return next_node_state(nid, N_ONLINE);
 }
 static __always_inline unsigned int next_memory_node(int nid)
 {
-	return next_node(nid, node_states[N_MEMORY]);
+	return next_node_state(nid, N_MEMORY);
 }
 
 static __always_inline void node_set_online(int nid)
@@ -481,6 +495,12 @@ static __always_inline int num_node_state(enum node_states state)
 #define for_each_node_state(node, __state) \
 	for ( (node) = 0; (node) == 0; (node) = 1)
 
+#define first_node_state(state)	0
+static __always_inline unsigned int next_node_state(int nid, enum node_states state)
+{
+	return MAX_NUMNODES;
+}
+
 #define first_online_node	0
 #define first_memory_node	0
 #define next_online_node(nid)	(MAX_NUMNODES)
-- 
2.53.1-Meta

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the inconsistent setting of N_MEMORY, N_NORMAL_MEMORY, and N_HIGH_MEMORY flags in various places. They are centralizing these updates in node_set/clear_memory_state() to make the code more consistent and easier to maintain. The behavior remains unchanged.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the overloaded meaning of N_MEMORY by clarifying that it should only mean a node has memory, and introducing N_MEMORY_COMMON to mean a node's memory is reachable via ordinary allocation or MM service. The author explained that every node with memory is common, so N_MEMORY_COMMON equals N_MEMORY and there is no behavioral change.
review_comments.raw_body:
N_MEMORY is overloaded with two meanings:
  1) a node has memory.
  2) a node's memory is reachable via ordinary allocation or
     an arbitrary MM service may use that memory.

Allow N_MEMORY to mean #1, and introduce N_MEMORY_COMMON to mean #2.

N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes contain "common memory" capable of being managed
arbitrarily by the kernel MM based solely on zone membership. Following
commits convert relevant N_MEMORY users to N_MEMORY_COMMON.

Add folio_is_common_memory() and page_is_common_memory() for MM services
that walk folios. Following commits convert folio_is_zone_device() and
page_is_zone_device() callers accordingly.

Expose the state via `has_common_memory` so userspace can identify
the memory available to ordinary allocations and common MM services.

Add has_memory to the docs while we're here.

Every node with memory is common, so N_MEMORY_COMMON equals N_MEMORY
and there is no behavioral change.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node | 16 ++++++++++++++++
 Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst        |  8 +++++++-
 drivers/base/node.c                         |  2 ++
 include/linux/nodemask.h                    |  9 ++++++++-
 mm/internal.h                               | 15 +++++++++++++++
 mm/page_alloc.c                             |  3 +++
 6 files changed, 51 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node b/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node
index 2d0e023f22a71..a93de328f8fe8 100644
--- a/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node
+++ b/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-devices-node
@@ -10,6 +10,15 @@ Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
 Description:
 		Nodes that are online.
 
+What:		/sys/devices/system/node/has_memory
+Date:		December 2012
+Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
+Description:
+		Nodes that have memory.
+
+		This memory may or may not be reachable via standard
+		allocations, see has_common_memory for details.
+
 What:		/sys/devices/system/node/has_normal_memory
 Date:		October 2002
 Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
@@ -29,6 +38,13 @@ Description:
 		Nodes that have regular or high memory.
 		Depends on CONFIG_HIGHMEM.
 
+What:		/sys/devices/system/node/has_common_memory
+Date:		November 2026
+Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
+Description:
+		Nodes whose memory ordinary allocations may use without
+		requesting the node explicitly.
+
 What:		/sys/devices/system/node/nodeX
 Date:		October 2002
 Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
diff --git a/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst b/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
index 2e67e8b23a994..fd5c5d136180f 100644
--- a/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
+++ b/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
@@ -168,7 +168,12 @@ nodes with particular properties as defined by ``enum node_states``:
   The node has regular or high memory. When ``CONFIG_HIGHMEM`` is disabled
   aliased to ``N_NORMAL_MEMORY``.
 ``N_MEMORY``
-  The node has memory(regular, high, movable)
+  The node has online memory (regular, high, movable).  This is a topology and
+  accounting state. Presence in this mask does not mean ordinary allocations

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about migration targets being set to N_MEMORY instead of N_MEMORY_COMMON, which can lead to unusable destination nodes during partial offlining. The author agreed that the hot-unplug migration target-list should be restricted to N_MEMORY_COMMON and provided a patch with the necessary changes.
review_comments.raw_body:
do_migrate_range() / alloc_migration_target() is only capable of
allocating memory on N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes. The destination nodemask
presently starts with N_MEMORY and removes the source-node.

In the current code, if the destination mask becomes empty, the source
node is restored to allow migration during partial offlining.

Consider this configuration:
  Node0 = N_MEMORY_COMMON
  Node1 = N_MEMORY, not N_MEMORY_COMMON

Node 1 keeps the destination mask non-empty, despite being unreachable.
This leaves migration with no usable destination because the source
node is not an eligible allocation target.

Restrict the hot-unplug migration target-list to N_MEMORY_COMMON so it
reflects the nodes the allocator can reach.

All memory is common at this point - behavior is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/memory_hotplug.c | 8 ++++----
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/memory_hotplug.c b/mm/memory_hotplug.c
index 490f400498f14..29ff2c46499b3 100644
--- a/mm/memory_hotplug.c
+++ b/mm/memory_hotplug.c
@@ -1904,7 +1904,7 @@ static void do_migrate_range(unsigned long start_pfn, unsigned long end_pfn)
 		folio_put(folio);
 	}
 	if (!list_empty(&source)) {
-		nodemask_t nmask = node_states[N_MEMORY];
+		nodemask_t nmask = node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON];
 		struct migration_target_control mtc = {
 			.nmask = &nmask,
 			.gfp_mask = GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_MOVABLE | __GFP_RETRY_MAYFAIL,
@@ -1919,9 +1919,9 @@ static void do_migrate_range(unsigned long start_pfn, unsigned long end_pfn)
 		mtc.nid = folio_nid(list_first_entry(&source, struct folio, lru));
 
 		/*
-		 * try to allocate from a different node but reuse this node
-		 * if there are no other online nodes to be used (e.g. we are
-		 * offlining a part of the only existing node)
+		 * try to allocate from a different common node but reuse this
+		 * node if there are no other common nodes to be used (e.g. we
+		 * are offlining a part of the only common node)
 		 */
 		node_clear(mtc.nid, nmask);
 		if (nodes_empty(nmask))

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that there are two mechanisms to enforce the 'common memory only' rule: zonelists built from N_MEMORY_COMMON and checks at call sites using node_state() or folio_is_common_memory(). However, he found inconsistencies where some paths use both mechanisms, while others use only one. He requested clarification on which mechanism is responsible for each path, particularly when a non-common node gets its own zonelist.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Gregory,

I've browsed through the serie, I'll go into detail in each patch
in the following days, for now I have one general question.

I wonder how the "common memory only" rule is enforced ?

As far as I read it, there're 2 ways:
1. The zonelist, you build them from N_MEMORY_COMMON, so non-common
   node isn't in any zonelist.
2. A check at the call site, e.g. node_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON) or
   folio_is_common_memory()


Code reaches a node's memory in 3 ways: zonelist, node id, or by folio.
I couldn't find a statement of which mechanism is responsible for which
kind of path.

I see some consistent issues,
1. zonelist paths are covered by way number 1. Some of them also carry
   way number 2, some don't
2. node id and folio paths can only be covered by way number 2. Some entry
   points have the check, and some do not.

I can't tell when a call site has no check is deliberate or missed.
This matters once non-common node gets its own zonelist, as patch 4 metioned I think?

Could you clarify the rule ? e.g. which zonelist users must filter on N_MEMORY_COMMON
themselves? and why the zonelist alone is not enough for them ?
Whether every path that takes a node id or a folio must check N_MEMORY_COMMON, and
which ones are left for the feature bits in phase 3 ?

Let's get the rule settled down and make it as the foundation as well as phase 2 and
phase 3 ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that the new code may lead to uneven or smaller-than-requested huge page pools due to delayed node addition, and suggested placing nodes_and() inside the loop to restore the original behavior.
review_comments.raw_body:
For a global request the caller passes &node_states[N_MEMORY], so before this patch
the grow loop read the live mask on every alloc_pool_huge_folio().
Now the mask is sampled once, before the loop.

The loop drops hugetlb_lock and can run for a long time. If a node gets its first
memoroy in that window, the old code would start using it. The new code won't, until
the next write to nr_hugepages.

So the pool can end up uneven, or smaller than requested if the other nodes are full.

I think the nodes_and() should be placed inside the loop to keep the old behavior ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: reviewer questioned whether the patch introduces significant cache pressure and noted that the new code writes to node_states[] multiple times for each onlined block, suggesting a potential optimization opportunity
review_comments.raw_body:
Um, so I am not sure how much cache pressure this will add, I assume it's small ?

Just want to point out that the old code only wrote these bits for a node's first
memory. THis now does up to 3 set_bit() calls on node_states[] for every onlined block.
The result is the same, but node_states[] is __read_mostly. A test-before-set in the helper
would keep the old behavior, or if you would like to keep it, please address in commit message.

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

review_comments.author: Richard Cheng
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that the patch uses two helper functions for_each_common_node and for_each_non_common_node, whereas another function for_each_populated_zone_state in the same patch uses a single 'if (!cond) ; else' form instead. He questioned whether this difference is due to avoiding -Wdangling-else warnings or if it should be consistent with for_each_populated_zone_state.
review_comments.raw_body:
A question on consistency. This one is a single for statement, with 2 new helper functions.
for_each_populated_zone_state() in the same patch uses "if (!cond) ; else" form instead.

Both forms keep a caller's else correct. The only difference I can find is that the if/else
form give a -Wdangling-else warning when the loop is the unbraced body of an if.

Is that the reason for the 2 helper function here? If the warning doesn't matter, this could
use the same short form and drop the 2 functions. If it does matter, should
for_each_populated_zone_state() be a single statement too ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary:
The author acknowledged that the existing code already handles the two cases mentioned by Richard Cheng and explained that the series largely modifies these locations to use N_MEMORY_COMMON instead.

The author is addressing concerns about how to reach a node's folios/pages, specifically in the context of page allocator freelists and pfn walks. They provided three categories of methods: kernel structures (page tables, VMAs, etc.), pfn walks (memory hot-unplug, contiguous allocation, DAMON), and the page allocator itself (freelists).

The author acknowledged that some filtering is already done by existing code and agreed to add additional filtering in a later patch to reduce complexity.

The author is addressing concerns about premature changes in the patch series. They acknowledge that some code should be moved to later phases (N_MEMORY_PRIVATE and N_MEMORY_FEATURE) and will restructure the current phase to handle cases for walking zonelists, nodelists, folios, and private zonelists in order.
review_comments.raw_body:
Those are essentially the two cases, which are already present in the
code in one shape or another in the existing shape:

   node_state(nid, N_MEMORY);
        or
   folio_is_zone_device(folio)

With the exception of one or two places, the series largely modifies
these locations to use N_MEMORY_COMMON instead (or in addition, in the
case of zone device).  There are a few places we add common checks where
zone device checks were not already present (because they were missing
or did not apply, usually PMD scenarios).

---

Being a bit more precise: How do we reach a node's folios/pages?

 1) through some kernel structure, obvious examples:
    - page tables
    - VMAs / pagemaps / xarrays
    - LRUs

 2) pfn walks
    - memory hot-unplug
    - contiguous allocation
    - DAMON

 3) page allocator
    - freelists (page allocator)
    Sort of its own category since you ask it for folios from a node

---

Some of this is obfuscated by the fact that the existing code already
does this filtering for you.

I suppose I have some premature changes to add additional filtering
where it isn't needed yet to reduce the complexity of later patches,
but I can see why this is confusing when introduced by itself.

Consider this:

-       for_each_zone_zonelist_nodemask(zone, z, zonelist,
-                                       gfp_zone(gfp_mask), nodemask) {
+       for_each_zone_node_state(zone, z, zonelist, gfp_zone(gfp_mask),
+                                nodemask, N_MEMORY_COMMON) {

This is a bit of a preparatory change to later convert this to:

+       for_each_zone_node_state(zone, z, zonelist, gfp_zone(gfp_mask),
+                                nodemask, N_MEMORY_RECLAIM) {

It looks like we're filtering by N_MEMORY_COMMON, but we're actually
iterating the fallback zonelist (constructed from N_MEMORY_COMMON)

  struct zonelist *zonelist = node_zonelist(numa_node_id(), sc.gfp_mask);

Later we update this node_zonelist() call to determine whether the
private nodelist should be walked, at which point you do have to filter
for service support.

---

So:
  1) If you're walking the normal zonelists, you're already filtered

  2) If you're walking nodelists, you need to filter on N_MEMORY_COMMON

  3) If you're operating on folios, you need to check common_memory()

  4) If you're walking the private zonelist, filter on N_MEMORY_COMMON


So let me do this:
  1) i'll restructure this phase to omit premature changes like above
     (they'll move into N_MEMORY_PRIVATE and N_MEMORY_<FEATURE> commits).

  2) I'll restructure N_MEMORY_COMMON commits here to handle cases 1-3
     above in that order, and that'll hopefully clear up the confusion.

-- 
~Gregory
